issue.title: A leading unknown plan-header key is silently ignored instead of diagnosed
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.1 (epic sase-g4). Not caused by that epic: this is pre-existing parser behaviour that the epic's new header-invalid validation rule made visible, because the rule only fires when the parser reports a problem.

sdd_plan_header_block_problem() -> first_header_candidate() (crates/sase_core/src/plan/artifact_link.rs:907) requires the block to START with a KNOWN section key. A bolded-key bullet whose key is unknown, appearing first, is therefore not recognized as the start of a header block at all: the whole block is classified MISSING and no diagnostic is emitted. The same unknown key placed after a known one is correctly rejected.

Reproduced at master be25ef5b4 with sase-core-rs 0.18.4 installed:

  leading unknown key      -> disposition=MISSING, reason=None
  unknown key after known  -> disposition=INVALID, reason='unknown `NOPE` section inside plan header block'

(both documents identical apart from bullet order; probe used sase.sdd.plan_header_block.parse_plan_header_block on a tale document whose bullets were '- **NOPE:** [x](x.md)' and '- **PARENT:** [p](p.md)').

Impact is small but real: it is exactly the shape a hand-authoring agent produces (a made-up section name at the top of the block), and it is the one case where sase-g4's new rule does not catch a hand-authored header block. The plan text a user sees looks like a provenance block and is silently treated as prose.

Scope: decide the intended contract and implement it. Diagnosing a leading bolded-key bullet that looks like a header section but names an unknown key would close the gap; the risk to weigh is false positives on ordinary prose bullets that happen to start with a bolded word followed by a link, so the detection needs to be narrow (bolded key immediately followed by ':' and a single Markdown link, at the document's leading-block position). Whichever way it lands, pin it with a Rust test.

Repo: sase-core (open with 'sase repo open sase-core'). If the decision is to diagnose it, the fix also needs a floor bump here once released.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d), closed as one group. Each was verified as described but none is currently costing anyone anything: sase-fm — 'note' really is missing from _MUTATING_VERBS in src/sase/main/bead_fast_path.py (confirmed at HEAD: the frozenset is {'+1','close','create','open','ref','rm','update'}), but it is a sandbox-guard bypass with no observed bad write, so it protects tests from themselves rather than protecting production state. sase-fn — unreachable epic-path code in run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py; a cleanup with zero behavioral consequence either way. sase-gb — confirmed at HEAD that src/sase/sdd/_write.py still projects (line 85) before validating (line 95), but the bead itself records that sase-g4's approval gate rejects a malformed plan before this path runs, making it defence in depth against a future non-approval caller. sase-gd — the dry-run 'Archived' line does overclaim, but sase-g4 already removed the specific defect that line once hid. sase-ga — a leading unknown plan-header key going undiagnosed is, in the bead's own words, 'small but real', and the fix lives cross-repo in sase-core with a false-positive risk on ordinary prose bullets. Reopen any of these with a +1 if one actually bites — sase-fm in particular is worth a +1 the moment an unsandboxed 'sase bead note' is seen writing outside a test's store.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: defence-in-depth, dead code, or misleading-but-harmless output with no currently-reproducing user-visible failure. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
